subject: WL
overview: Spanish 1B finishes Spanish I, moving from Novice Mid toward Novice High: restaurants, home and chores, clothing and shopping, travel in the preterite, community service, movies and technology. Keep the 1A routine of daily Spanish (date, weather, a quick question) and add one new structure per week: model it, drill it briefly online (Conjuguemos or StudySpanish), then use it in a real conversation or writing task. Answers below give the correct Spanish so a non-fluent parent can check; in speaking, reward communication first and correct one pattern at a time.

weeks.prep: Pull out the 1A can-do checklist. Set a place setting (plate, glass, cup, fork, knife, spoon, napkin, bowl, tablecloth, salt and pepper). Write a 15-item 1A diagnostic quiz (ser, gustar, -ar/-er/-ir present, tener, ir a, dates/time).
misconceptions: Saying 'el camarero' for women. Use la camarera (or el/la mesero/a in Mexico).
Ordering with 'Yo quiero' only. In restaurants use '¿Me trae…?' or 'Quisiera…' — more polite.

days.guide: Hold a 3-minute conversation about summer, family and likes; give the diagnostic quiz and note weak areas.

questions.q: Answer: ¿Qué te gusta hacer en el verano?
questions.a: En el verano me gusta ___ (infinitive), e.g., nadar y leer.

questions.q: Answer: ¿Cuántos hermanos tienes?

days.guide: Learn 12 table words; set the table naming items: Pongo el tenedor a la izquierda del plato.

questions.q: Say: 'I put the knife to the right of the plate.'
questions.a: Pongo el cuchillo a la derecha del plato.

questions.q: What is 'la servilleta'?

days.guide: Learn main dishes, desserts and drinks (el bistec, el pollo asado, el arroz, la ensalada, el flan, el helado, el pastel, el agua mineral, el té helado); build a three-course menu.

questions.q: What is 'el flan'?
How do you say 'main dish'?

days.guide: Practice requests with you as camarero: ¿Me trae…?, ¿Me puede traer…?, ¿Algo más?, La cuenta, por favor.

questions.q: Ask the waiter to bring you a spoon.
questions.a: ¿Me trae una cuchara, por favor? (or ¿Me puede traer una cuchara?)

days.guide: Give the vocabulary quiz; set two goals from the diagnostic.

questions.q: Translate: 'Anything else?' 'No, thank you. The check, please.'
questions.a: ¿Algo más? —No, gracias. La cuenta, por favor.

weeks.assessment_key: Restaurant vocabulary quiz key: el plato (plate), el vaso (glass), la taza (cup), el tenedor (fork), el cuchillo (knife), la cuchara (spoon), la servilleta (napkin), el tazón (bowl), el mantel (tablecloth), la sal, la pimienta, el camarero/la camarera (waiter/waitress), el plato principal (main dish), el postre (dessert), la cuenta (check). Phrases: ¿Me trae…, por favor? (Can you bring me…?); ¿Algo más? (Anything else?). 80% proficient. Diagnostic conversation: 3 minutes using present tense, gustar and ir a; note gaps for goals.

weeks.prep: Conjuguemos account; plan a real family meal for day 3. A short restaurant scene video in Spanish (textbook video or YouTube).
misconceptions: Conjugating venir as regular: 'yo veno.' The yo form is vengo; it is also e→ie: vienes, viene, vienen (venimos, venís unchanged).
Saying 'La comida es rica' when you mean it tastes good right now. 'Está rica' = it tastes delicious (this dish); 'es rica' can describe a type of food or mean rich (wealthy) for people.

days.guide: Teach venir forms; Conjuguemos to 90%.

questions.q: Conjugate venir for yo and ellos.
Complete: Nosotros ___ a las ocho.

days.guide: Write dinner invitations and who comes from where.

questions.q: Write: 'My aunt comes from San Diego on Saturday.'
questions.a: Mi tía viene de San Diego el sábado.

days.guide: Describe five foods during a real meal.

questions.q: Say: 'The salsa is very spicy.'
Say: 'The cake is sweet and delicious.'
questions.a: El pastel está dulce y delicioso.

days.guide: Watch a restaurant scene; list what each customer orders and how they describe it.

questions.q: If a customer says 'La sopa está un poco salada,' what's the complaint?
questions.a: The soup is a little salty.

days.guide: Give the venir and description quiz.

questions.q: Ask: 'Are you coming to dinner?'

weeks.assessment_key: Venir quiz: vengo, vienes, viene, venimos, venís, vienen. Samples: Mis abuelos (venir) de Texas → vienen; ¿(venir) tú a la fiesta? → vienes; Nosotros (venir) a las seis → venimos; Yo (venir) en coche → vengo. Food words: delicioso, picante (spicy), salado (salty), dulce (sweet), rico (tasty). 80% passing.

weeks.prep: Make 20 sentence cards mixing ser and estar uses. StudySpanish.com ser/estar lesson.
misconceptions: Using estar for professions: 'Está doctora.' Occupation uses ser: Es doctora.
Using ser for location of things/people: location uses estar (El restaurante está en la calle Main). Exception: events — La fiesta es en mi casa.

days.guide: Teach DOCTOR and PLACE; sort 20 cards.

questions.q: Which verb for 'Ella ___ abogada'? Why?
Which verb for 'Yo ___ nervioso hoy'? Why?

days.guide: Study meaning-change adjectives: es aburrido (is boring) vs está aburrido (is bored); es listo (is clever) vs está listo (is ready); es rico (is rich) vs está rico (tastes good); write 6 pairs.

questions.q: Translate: 'The movie is boring' and 'I am bored.'
questions.a: La película es aburrida. Estoy aburrido/a.

questions.q: What's the difference between 'es listo' and 'está listo'?
questions.a: Es listo = he is clever; está listo = he is ready.

days.guide: Describe a meal: what food is (ser) and how it tastes today (estar), plus diners' feelings.

questions.q: Write: 'Paella is a typical dish; today it is delicious.'
questions.a: La paella es un plato típico; hoy está deliciosa.

days.guide: Complete the StudySpanish lesson and exercises.

questions.q: Choose: ¿Dónde ___ los baños? (son/están)

days.guide: Give the 25-item quiz.

questions.q: Choose: ___ las diez de la noche. (Son/Están)

weeks.assessment_key: 25-item quiz guide: ser for DOCTOR — Description (permanent traits), Occupation, Characteristic, Time/date, Origin, Relationship; estar for PLACE — Position, Location, Action (progressive), Condition, Emotion. Samples: Mi madre ___ profesora (es); La sopa ___ fría (está); ___ las dos (son); Nosotros ___ cansados (estamos); El museo ___ cerca (está); Él ___ mi primo (es); Ellos ___ de Chile (son); Yo ___ comiendo (estoy); Hoy ___ lunes (es); La fiesta ___ en el parque (es). 20/25 = 80%.

weeks.prep: Print an authentic menu from a Spanish or Mexican restaurant's website. Write cue cards template. Read about tapas, comida corrida and sobremesa.
misconceptions: Assuming tipping customs match the U.S. In Spain tips are small or optional (service is included); in Mexico about 10–15% is common.
Using tú with the waiter. Use usted: ¿Qué me recomienda?

days.guide: Read about tapas, comida corrida and sobremesa; compare meal times with yours.

questions.q: What is 'la sobremesa'?
questions.a: Relaxing and talking at the table after a meal.

questions.q: When do many Spaniards eat dinner?
questions.a: Late — around 9 to 10 p.m. (lunch, the main meal, around 2–3 p.m.).

days.guide: Read the authentic menu; answer 10 questions about dishes and prices.

questions.q: What are 'entradas' or 'entrantes' on a menu?

days.guide: Write cue cards for the role-play.

questions.q: Ask the waiter what he recommends.

days.guide: Perform the role-play from arrival to paying.

questions.q: Say: 'The chicken is delicious, thank you.'

days.guide: Give the unit 1 test.

questions.q: Translate: 'My friends come from the restaurant.'

weeks.assessment_key: Role-play rubric (1–4 each): greeting and seating, ordering with polite requests and usted (¿Qué me recomienda? Quisiera… ¿Me trae…?), describing food with ser/estar, asking for and paying la cuenta, comprehensibility. Unit 1 test: restaurant listening, menu reading, venir conjugation, ser vs estar. Culture: tapas = small shared plates in Spain; comida corrida = affordable fixed-price multi-course lunch in Mexico; sobremesa = time spent talking at the table after a meal; main meal in Spain around 2–3 p.m., dinner around 9–10 p.m.

weeks.prep: Floor plan paper, sticky notes. Vocabulary: la cocina, la sala, el comedor, el dormitorio, el baño, el garaje, el sótano, el jardín, la escalera, el pasillo; furniture: la cama, la cómoda, el armario, la alfombra, el sofá, la lámpara, el escritorio, el estante, la mesita, el espejo, la cortina, el sillón, la silla, la mesa, el televisor.
misconceptions: Colors not agreeing. Rojo/roja/rojos/rojas; azul/azules (no gender); marrón/marrones; naranja and rosa often don't change.
Placing color before the noun. Colors follow nouns: la alfombra roja.

days.guide: Learn 10 rooms; draw and label a floor plan.

questions.q: How do you say 'the kitchen' and 'the living room'?

days.guide: Learn 15 furniture items; label your bedroom.

questions.q: What is 'la cómoda'?

days.guide: Learn colors with agreement; describe 10 items.

questions.q: Write: 'The rug is red and the curtains are yellow.'
questions.a: La alfombra es roja y las cortinas son amarillas.

days.guide: Write a 10-sentence bedroom description with hay, estar + prepositions, colors.

questions.q: Write: 'The lamp is on top of the desk.'
questions.a: La lámpara está encima del escritorio.

days.guide: Give the house vocabulary quiz.

questions.q: Translate: 'There are two black chairs.'

weeks.assessment_key: House vocabulary quiz: 10 rooms, 15 furniture items with articles, colors with agreement. Samples: the green curtains → las cortinas verdes; the white bed → la cama blanca; the blue lamps → las lámparas azules; 'In my bedroom there is a desk next to the bed' → En mi dormitorio hay un escritorio al lado de la cama. 80% proficient.

weeks.prep: Photos of rooms or Spanish real-estate ads (e.g., from Idealista or Inmuebles24).
misconceptions: Saying 'más bueno' and 'más malo.' Use mejor and peor.
Using 'que' with tan. Equal comparisons use tan… como: tan grande como.

days.guide: Teach más/menos…que, tan…como; compare 10 pairs.

questions.q: Compare: the sofa (big) vs the chair.
questions.a: El sofá es más grande que la silla.

questions.q: Write: 'The lamp is as tall as the shelf.'
questions.a: La lámpara es tan alta como el estante.

days.guide: Teach mejor, peor, mayor, menor; compare family.

questions.q: Write: 'My sister is younger than me.'
questions.a: Mi hermana es menor que yo.

questions.q: Write: 'My dad cooks better than I do.'
questions.a: Mi papá cocina mejor que yo.

days.guide: Teach el/la más… de; write superlatives.

questions.q: Write: 'My room is the smallest in the house.'
questions.a: Mi cuarto es el más pequeño de la casa.

days.guide: Read three apartment ads; compare in 8 sentences.

questions.q: What does 'tres dormitorios, dos baños' mean?

days.guide: Give the comparisons quiz.

questions.q: Translate: 'She is the best student in the class.'
questions.a: Ella es la mejor estudiante de la clase.

weeks.assessment_key: Comparisons quiz samples: The kitchen is bigger than the bathroom → La cocina es más grande que el baño; My room is as small as yours → Mi cuarto es tan pequeño como el tuyo; My brother is older than I → Mi hermano es mayor que yo; This apartment is the best in the city → Este apartamento es el mejor de la ciudad; The sofa is less comfortable than the armchair → El sofá es menos cómodo que el sillón. 80% proficient.

weeks.prep: Boot-chart template (draw a boot around yo, tú, él, ellos forms), Conjuguemos stem-changer practice.
misconceptions: Changing the stem in nosotros: 'puedemos.' Nosotros and vosotros keep the original stem: podemos.
Changing the ending vowel instead of the stem: 'dormo.' The change is in the stem: duermo.

days.guide: Teach the boot; conjugate poder and dormir.

questions.q: Conjugate dormir for yo and nosotros.
Which forms don't change in a boot verb?

days.guide: Add costar, volver, encontrar, almorzar, jugar (u→ue); Conjuguemos drill.

questions.q: Conjugate jugar for tú.
Complete: ¿Cuánto ___ la lámpara? (costar)

days.guide: Survey family: ¿Cuántas horas duermes? ¿A qué hora vuelves a casa? Graph.

questions.q: Report: 'My dad sleeps seven hours.'

days.guide: Write 10 puedo/no puedo sentences about the house.

questions.q: Write: 'I can't play ball in the living room.'
questions.a: No puedo jugar a la pelota en la sala.

days.guide: Give the o→ue quiz.

questions.q: Translate: 'We can eat lunch at noon.'

weeks.assessment_key: Stem-changer quiz: poder — puedo, puedes, puede, podemos, podéis, pueden; dormir — duermo, duermes, duerme, dormimos, dormís, duermen; jugar — juego, juegas, juega, jugamos, jugáis, juegan. Samples: ¿Cuánto (costar) los zapatos? → cuestan; Nosotros (volver) a las cinco → volvemos; Yo (almorzar) a la una → almuerzo; Ella no (encontrar) sus llaves → encuentra. 80% passing.

weeks.prep: Chore chart. Chores: hacer la cama, lavar los platos, sacar la basura, pasar la aspiradora, poner la mesa, quitar la mesa, limpiar el baño, cortar el césped, dar de comer al perro, lavar la ropa, sacudir los muebles, cocinar, arreglar el cuarto, planchar.
misconceptions: Using the infinitive as a command: 'Lavar los platos.' The tú command is the él form: Lava los platos.
Forgetting irregulars: 'hace la cama' (he makes) vs 'haz la cama' (make the bed!).

days.guide: Learn 14 chores; make a family chore chart.

questions.q: How do you say 'to take out the trash'?
What does 'pasar la aspiradora' mean?

days.guide: Teach regular tú commands (= él form); write a command for each chore.

questions.q: Command: wash the dishes.
Command: clean the bathroom.

days.guide: Teach di, haz, ve, pon, sal, sé, ten, ven; 20-item practice.

questions.q: Command: set the table.
Command: go to your room.

days.guide: Play Simón dice with 20 commands; do three chores as commanded.

questions.q: Command: come to the kitchen.

days.guide: Give the commands quiz.

questions.q: Command: make the bed.

weeks.assessment_key: Commands quiz key: regular — limpia, lava, saca, pasa, cocina, come, bebe, escribe, barre; irregular — decir → di, hacer → haz, ir → ve, poner → pon, salir → sal, ser → sé, tener → ten, venir → ven. Samples: Make your bed → Haz tu cama; Put the table (set it) → Pon la mesa; Take out the trash → Saca la basura; Come here → Ven aquí; Be good → Sé bueno. Chore role-play: gives and follows 5 commands correctly.

weeks.prep: Phone for the home tour. A busy-house illustration (search 'Spanish present progressive picture'). Read about homes in Spain and Latin America.
misconceptions: Using -ando with -er/-ir verbs: 'comando.' -ar → -ando; -er/-ir → -iendo (comiendo, escribiendo).
Missing the irregulars: leer → leyendo, dormir → durmiendo.

days.guide: Teach estar + -ando/-iendo; describe what family members are doing now.

questions.q: Say: 'My mom is reading.'
Say: 'We are cleaning the kitchen.'

days.guide: Describe a busy house picture in 10 sentences.

questions.q: Say: 'The baby is sleeping.'

days.guide: Read about homes; write five comparisons.

questions.q: What is an 'azotea'?
questions.a: A flat rooftop terrace used for laundry, plants or gathering.

questions.q: Write: 'In Spain many families live in apartments.'
questions.a: En España muchas familias viven en pisos (apartamentos).

days.guide: Record a 2-minute home tour.

questions.q: Say: 'This is the living room. It is bigger than the kitchen.'
questions.a: Esta es la sala. Es más grande que la cocina.

days.guide: Give the unit 2 test.

questions.q: Translate: 'My brother is washing the dishes.'
questions.a: Mi hermano está lavando los platos.

weeks.assessment_key: Home tour rubric (1–4): 2 minutes, names rooms and furniture, uses comparisons (más/menos…que), mentions chores with present tense or commands, uses estar + prepositions, pronunciation. Unit 2 test: house vocabulary, comparisons, o→ue verbs, tú commands, present progressive (estoy limpiando, está leyendo, están durmiendo). Culture: interior patios (Spain/colonial Latin America), rooftop azoteas, many families live in apartments (pisos) in cities.

weeks.prep: Closet items, catalog photos, a short teen fashion blog in Spanish. Vocabulary: la camisa, la camiseta, los pantalones, los jeans/vaqueros, la falda, el vestido, los zapatos, los tenis, las botas, la chaqueta, el abrigo, el suéter, la gorra, el sombrero, los calcetines, la sudadera, los pantalones cortos, el traje de baño, la bufanda, los guantes.
misconceptions: Using 'usar' and 'llevar' interchangeably is fine, but 'llevar' is the standard for wearing; don't use 'tener' for wearing.
Color agreement with plurals: los pantalones negros.

days.guide: Learn 20 clothing words; label closet items.

questions.q: How do you say 'the jacket' and 'the socks'?

days.guide: Describe what five family members wear with llevar + colors.

questions.q: Write: 'My dad is wearing blue jeans and a white shirt.'
questions.a: Mi papá lleva unos jeans azules y una camisa blanca.

days.guide: Connect weather to clothes; write 8 sentences.

questions.q: Write: 'When it's cold, I wear a coat.'
questions.a: Cuando hace frío, llevo un abrigo.

questions.q: Write: 'When it's hot, I wear shorts.'
questions.a: Cuando hace calor, llevo pantalones cortos.

days.guide: Read a teen fashion blog; list items and opinions.

questions.q: What does 'está de moda' mean?

days.guide: Give the clothing quiz with listening.

questions.q: Translate: 'She wears a green cap.'

weeks.assessment_key: Clothing quiz: 20 items with articles; listening — child identifies what a person is wearing. Samples: She is wearing a red dress → Ella lleva un vestido rojo; I wear boots when it's cold → Llevo botas cuando hace frío; a black jacket → una chaqueta negra. 80% proficient.

weeks.prep: Conjuguemos e→ie practice.
misconceptions: Changing nosotros: 'queremos' (correct), not 'quieremos.'
Confusing pensar + infinitive (plan to) with pensar en (think about).

days.guide: Teach e→ie verbs in the boot; Conjuguemos drill.

questions.q: Conjugate querer for yo and nosotros.
Conjugate empezar for la clase.

days.guide: Write 10 preference sentences.

questions.q: Write: 'I prefer the red shirt, but my brother wants the blue one.'
questions.a: Prefiero la camisa roja, pero mi hermano quiere la azul.

days.guide: Use pensar + infinitive for three plans; compare with ir a.

questions.q: Write: 'I plan to buy new shoes.'

days.guide: Discuss clothes you want, prefer and plan to buy.

questions.q: Ask: 'What do you prefer, the jacket or the sweater?'
questions.a: ¿Qué prefieres, la chaqueta o el suéter?

days.guide: Give the e→ie quiz with mixed o→ue items.

questions.q: Translate: 'They don't understand the question.'

weeks.assessment_key: Quiz key: pensar — pienso, piensas, piensa, pensamos, pensáis, piensan; querer — quiero, quieres, quiere, queremos, queréis, quieren; preferir — prefiero, prefieres, prefiere, preferimos, preferís, prefieren; empezar — empiezo…; entender — entiendo…; cerrar — cierro… Mixed o→ue: puedo, duermes, vuelven. Samples: La tienda (cerrar) a las nueve → cierra; Nosotros (preferir) la camisa azul → preferimos; ¿Tú (entender)? → entiendes. 80% proficient.

weeks.prep: Price tags on household items, a currency converter website (check current rates). Demonstratives chart.
misconceptions: Using 'doscientos' with feminine nouns. Hundreds agree: doscientas camisas.
Saying 'un mil.' 1,000 is mil; 1,000,000 is un millón (de): un millón de dólares.

days.guide: Teach demonstratives at three distances; 12 sentences.

questions.q: Say: 'This shirt and those shoes (over there).'
Say: 'those pants (near you).'

days.guide: Teach 100–1,000,000; read 20 prices.

questions.q: Write 750 in words.
Write 2.500 in words.

days.guide: Learn currencies of eight countries; convert three prices with a current rate.

questions.q: What is the currency of Guatemala? Of Peru?

days.guide: Practice ¿Cuánto cuesta(n)? with tagged items.

questions.q: Ask how much these boots cost and answer 'They cost 80 dollars.'

days.guide: Give the demonstratives and number dictation quiz.

questions.q: Write 500 and 900.

weeks.assessment_key: Quiz key: este/esta/estos/estas (this/these, near speaker), ese/esa/esos/esas (that/those, near listener), aquel/aquella/aquellos/aquellas (that/those over there). Numbers: 100 cien, 101 ciento uno, 200 doscientos, 300 trescientos, 400 cuatrocientos, 500 quinientos, 600 seiscientos, 700 setecientos, 800 ochocientos, 900 novecientos, 1.000 mil, 2.000 dos mil, 1.000.000 un millón. Dictation samples: 550 quinientos cincuenta; 1.975 mil novecientos setenta y cinco; 25.000 veinticinco mil. Currencies: México — peso; España — euro; Guatemala — quetzal; Perú — sol; Costa Rica — colón; Argentina — peso; Colombia — peso; Ecuador and El Salvador — U.S. dollar; Venezuela — bolívar; Paraguay — guaraní; Honduras — lempira. 80% proficient.

weeks.prep: Play money, clothing items. Read about the Chichicastenango market (Guatemala) and El Rastro (Madrid). A short video on Guatemalan Maya weaving (huipiles).
misconceptions: Bargaining everywhere. Bargaining (regatear) is expected at many open-air markets and street stalls, not in department stores or fixed-price shops.
Saying 'Me queda bueno.' Use 'Me queda bien' (it fits well); 'Me queda grande/pequeño' for size.

days.guide: Learn store phrases; practice a fitting-room dialogue.

questions.q: A clerk asks '¿Qué talla usa?' What is she asking?
Say: 'These pants are too big on me.'

days.guide: Read about markets and when bargaining is appropriate.

questions.q: Where is bargaining usually acceptable?
questions.a: At open-air markets and street stalls, not in department stores or chain shops.

days.guide: Watch the weaving video; write five sentences about huipiles.

questions.q: What is a huipil?
questions.a: A traditional handwoven tunic/blouse worn by Maya women; its patterns can show the weaver's village and beliefs.

days.guide: Role-play a store purchase and market bargaining with play money.

questions.q: Bargain: 'It's very expensive. Can you give me a discount?'
questions.a: Es muy caro. ¿Me puede dar un descuento?

days.guide: Give the shopping listening quiz.

questions.q: What does 'barato' mean?

weeks.assessment_key: Shopping role-play rubric (1–4): clerk/customer phrases (¿En qué puedo servirle? ¿Qué talla usa? Me queda bien/grande), asks and states prices, uses demonstratives, bargains politely (¿Me puede dar un descuento? Es muy caro), closing. Listening quiz: identifies item, size, color, price and whether it fits from a dialogue. Culture: Chichicastenango — large Maya market in the Guatemalan highlands (Thursdays and Sundays) with textiles, masks, produce; El Rastro — Madrid's Sunday open-air flea market; huipil — handwoven blouse whose designs and colors often identify the weaver's community and carry symbolic meaning.

weeks.prep: Paper or slide software for a catalog. An authentic online store page in Spanish (e.g., a Spanish clothing retailer's site).
misconceptions: Copying store-page text. Write your own descriptions using structures learned.
Forgetting euros use a comma for decimals in Spain (19,99 €).

days.guide: Design a catalog page with 8 items, colors, sizes, prices.

questions.q: Write a price: 45 euros and 99 cents.
questions.a: cuarenta y cinco euros con noventa y nueve (céntimos).

days.guide: Write descriptions with demonstratives, comparisons and e→ie verbs.

questions.q: Write: 'These boots are better than those shoes.'
questions.a: Estas botas son mejores que esos zapatos.

days.guide: Read an authentic store page; answer questions.

questions.q: What does 'añadir a la cesta' mean on a store site?

days.guide: Present a 90-second TV shopping segment.

questions.q: Say: 'Do you want a modern style? This sweater is perfect.'
questions.a: ¿Quieres un estilo moderno? Este suéter es perfecto.

days.guide: Give the unit 3 test.

questions.q: Translate: 'That dress (over there) costs 300 dollars.'

weeks.assessment_key: Catalog project rubric (1–4): 8 items with colors, sizes and prices; descriptions use demonstratives, comparisons and e→ie verbs (e.g., 'Esta chaqueta es más cómoda que aquel abrigo. ¿Prefieres el color azul?'); accurate agreement; attractive layout; 90-second TV segment with enthusiasm and clear pronunciation. Unit 3 test: clothing, e→ie/o→ue, demonstratives, numbers to 1,000,000, shopping phrases.

weeks.prep: Conjuguemos preterite -ar practice; three store receipts.
misconceptions: Dropping accents: 'compro' (I buy) vs 'compró' (he bought). The accent changes meaning and tense.
Confusing nosotros forms. -ar nosotros is the same in present and preterite (hablamos); context (ayer) tells the tense.

days.guide: Teach preterite -ar endings; conjugate comprar, hablar, mirar.

questions.q: Conjugate hablar for yo and ella.
Conjugate mirar for ellos.

days.guide: Teach time expressions; write 10 sentences about last weekend.

questions.q: Write: 'Last night I studied Spanish.'
Write: 'Two days ago we bought shoes.'

days.guide: Identify present vs past from context in 15 sentences.

questions.q: Is 'Hablamos con el profesor ayer' present or past?

days.guide: Write what people bought and paid from receipts.

questions.q: Write: 'My mom paid 50 dollars.'

days.guide: Give the preterite -ar quiz.

questions.q: Translate: 'Did you (tú) buy the jacket?'

weeks.assessment_key: Preterite -ar quiz: comprar — compré, compraste, compró, compramos, comprasteis, compraron. Samples: Ayer yo (hablar) con mi abuela → hablé; Ellos (mirar) la tele anoche → miraron; ¿Tú (comprar) la camisa? → compraste; La semana pasada nosotros (caminar) al parque → caminamos; Ella (trabajar) el sábado → trabajó. 80% proficient.

weeks.prep: StudySpanish.com preterite exercises.
misconceptions: Applying the spelling change to all persons. It occurs only in the yo form: busqué but buscaste, buscó.
Forgetting why: c→qu and g→gu keep the hard sound before é; z→c because Spanish writes ce, not ze.

days.guide: Teach the spelling rules; practice 15 yo forms.

questions.q: Give the yo preterite of buscar, pagar and almorzar.
Why does 'pagar' become 'pagué'?
questions.a: To keep the hard g sound before e (ge would sound like h).

days.guide: Complete StudySpanish exercises; correct errors.

questions.q: Give the tú preterite of tocar.

days.guide: Write a 10-sentence shopping diary with five spelling-change verbs.

questions.q: Write: 'I arrived at the store and I looked for a gift.'
questions.a: Llegué a la tienda y busqué un regalo.

days.guide: Interview a family member about yesterday; record answers.

questions.q: Ask: 'What time did you arrive home?'

days.guide: Give the spelling-change quiz.

questions.q: Give the yo preterite of practicar.

weeks.assessment_key: Quiz key: -car → -qué (buscar → busqué, tocar → toqué, practicar → practiqué, sacar → saqué); -gar → -gué (pagar → pagué, llegar → llegué, jugar → jugué); -zar → -cé (empezar → empecé, almorzar → almorcé, organizar → organicé). Samples: Yo (llegar) tarde → llegué; Él (pagar) → pagó (no change); Yo (empezar) la tarea → empecé; Tú (jugar) → jugaste. 80% proficient.

weeks.prep: A shopping bag with items (a shirt, shoes, a book, socks).
misconceptions: Placing the pronoun after a conjugated verb: 'Compré la.' It goes before: La compré.
Choosing gender by the person, not the noun. The pronoun matches the object: los zapatos → los.

days.guide: Teach lo/la/los/las; replace objects in 15 sentences.

questions.q: Replace: Compré los zapatos.
Replace: Busco la chaqueta.

days.guide: Teach placement: before conjugated verb, or attached to infinitive/gerund (add accent on gerund).

questions.q: Rewrite two ways: Voy a comprar la falda.
questions.a: La voy a comprar. / Voy a comprarla.

questions.q: Rewrite: Estoy leyendo el libro.

days.guide: Answer your questions with pronouns.

questions.q: ¿Compraste los calcetines?
questions.a: Sí, los compré. (or No, no los compré.)

days.guide: Write a gift story with preterite and DOPs.

questions.q: Write: 'I bought a scarf for my mom. I bought it at the market.'
questions.a: Compré una bufanda para mi mamá. La compré en el mercado.

days.guide: Give the DOP quiz.

questions.q: Replace: ¿Dónde compraste el vestido?

weeks.assessment_key: DOP quiz samples: Compré la camisa → La compré; ¿Tienes los libros? → Sí, los tengo; Voy a comprar el regalo → Lo voy a comprar / Voy a comprarlo; Estoy lavando los platos → Los estoy lavando / Estoy lavándolos; ¿Viste a María? → Sí, la vi. 80% proficient.

weeks.prep: Semester flashcards, unit tests, Conjuguemos.
misconceptions: Mixing tenses mid-story. Decide if it's now (present) or completed past (preterite) and keep consistent.
Forgetting boot verbs on the exam. Review the boot chart before writing.

days.guide: Review units 1–2 with a practice test.

questions.q: Command your brother to set the table and take out the trash.
questions.a: Pon la mesa y saca la basura.

days.guide: Review units 3–4 with Conjuguemos.

questions.q: Translate: 'I prefer these jeans; I bought them yesterday.'
questions.a: Prefiero estos jeans; los compré ayer.

days.guide: 4-minute interview: home, chores, clothes, shopping trip.

questions.q: Answer: ¿Qué compraste la semana pasada?
questions.a: La semana pasada compré ___, e.g., unos tenis.

days.guide: Give the written exam.

questions.q: Conjugate dormir (present) for ellos and comprar (preterite) for yo.

days.guide: Complete a can-do checklist; set two goals.

questions.q: Write one goal.
questions.a: Example: 'Master preterite endings with 90% on Conjuguemos.'

weeks.assessment_key: Semester exam (suggested): Listening 10 (restaurant/shopping dialogues), Reading 10 (menu/apartment ad), Grammar 25 (venir, ser/estar, comparisons, o→ue/e→ie, tú commands, progressive, demonstratives, numbers, preterite -ar and spelling changes, DOPs), Writing 15 (12 sentences on home, chores, clothes and a past shopping trip — rubric for content, accuracy, variety). Oral interview rubric (1–4): comprehension, sentence-level answers, asks questions, uses present and preterite, pronunciation. 80% proficient.

weeks.prep: Travel photos, world map, a Spanish tourism brochure for Puerto Rico (Discover Puerto Rico has Spanish content).
misconceptions: Confusing 'visitar a' (people) and 'visitar' (places): Visité a mi abuela; Visité el museo.
Using present tense in past-trip sentences. Use the preterite: Nadé en el lago.

days.guide: Learn 20 vacation words; caption travel photos.

questions.q: What does 'bucear' mean?
How do you say 'amusement park'?

days.guide: Write 10 past-trip sentences with -ar preterite.

questions.q: Write: 'I took many photos.'
Write: 'We swam in the lake.'

days.guide: Read a Puerto Rico brochure; list five attractions.

questions.q: Name two attractions in Puerto Rico.
questions.a: El Viejo San Juan, El Morro, El Yunque rainforest, bioluminescent bays (e.g., Mosquito Bay in Vieques), beaches.

days.guide: Choose a dream destination; list ten activities.

questions.q: Write: 'In Costa Rica I can visit volcanoes.'
questions.a: En Costa Rica puedo visitar volcanes.

days.guide: Give the vacation vocabulary quiz.

questions.q: Translate: 'She bought souvenirs.'

weeks.assessment_key: Vacation vocabulary quiz: el museo, el parque de diversiones, el zoológico, el lago, las montañas, el mar, la playa, el estadio, el parque nacional, el monumento, tomar el sol, bucear, montar a caballo, pasear en bote, acampar, ir de pesca, visitar, sacar fotos, comprar recuerdos, el hotel. Samples: I sunbathed at the beach → Tomé el sol en la playa; We visited the zoo → Visitamos el zoológico. 80% proficient.

weeks.prep: Conjuguemos preterite -er/-ir practice.
misconceptions: Using -ar endings for -er/-ir verbs: 'comé.' Use comí, comió.
Forgetting the y in leer/oír/creer third person: leyó, leyeron (not leió).

days.guide: Teach shared -er/-ir endings; conjugate comer and salir.

questions.q: Conjugate salir for ella and ellos.
Conjugate comer for yo.

days.guide: Conjuguemos drill to 90%.

questions.q: Conjugate vivir for nosotros (preterite).

days.guide: Teach leyó/leyeron, oyó/oyeron; five sentences.

questions.q: Write: 'My sister read the brochure.'
Write: 'They heard the music.'

days.guide: Interview a parent about their best vacation.

questions.q: Ask: 'What did you eat on the trip?'

days.guide: Give the mixed regular preterite quiz.

questions.q: Translate: 'We left at seven and returned at ten.'
questions.a: Salimos a las siete y volvimos a las diez.

weeks.assessment_key: Quiz key: comer — comí, comiste, comió, comimos, comisteis, comieron; salir — salí, saliste, salió, salimos, salisteis, salieron; leer — leí, leíste, leyó, leímos, leísteis, leyeron; oír — oí, oíste, oyó, oímos, oísteis, oyeron. Samples: Ayer nosotros (beber) limonada → bebimos; Ellos (escribir) postales → escribieron; Mi padre (volver) tarde → volvió; ¿Tú (aprender) a bucear? → aprendiste. 80% proficient.

weeks.prep: Photo album. A Spanish Proficiency Exercises clip about a trip (UT Austin, e.g., 'Describe a trip').
misconceptions: Thinking 'fue' always means 'went.' Ir and ser share preterite forms: 'Fue a Madrid' (went) vs 'Fue divertido' (was).
Adding accents: fui, fue have no accent.

days.guide: Teach the shared forms; determine meaning in 15 sentences.

questions.q: Translate: 'Fui al zoológico. Fue muy divertido.'
questions.a: I went to the zoo. It was very fun.

questions.q: Conjugate ir (preterite) for nosotros.

days.guide: Write where family members went last summer and how it was.

questions.q: Write: 'My parents went to Mexico; it was fantastic.'
questions.a: Mis padres fueron a México; fue fantástico.

days.guide: Listen to a native speaker; note where they went and what they did.

questions.q: If you hear 'Fuimos a las montañas y acampamos,' what did they do?
questions.a: They went to the mountains and camped.

days.guide: Unscripted conversation with five follow-up questions.

questions.q: Ask: 'Where did you go and with whom?'

days.guide: Give the ir/ser quiz.

questions.q: Ask: 'How was the trip?'
questions.a: ¿Qué tal fue el viaje? (or ¿Cómo fue el viaje?)

weeks.assessment_key: Quiz key: ir/ser — fui, fuiste, fue, fuimos, fuisteis, fueron. Context items: 'Fuimos a la playa' = we went; 'El viaje fue fantástico' = was; 'Ellos fueron al museo' = went; '¿Qué tal fue?' = how was it. Conversation rubric (1–4): describes a past trip in the preterite, asks/answers 5 follow-up questions (¿Adónde fuiste? ¿Con quién? ¿Qué hiciste? ¿Qué comiste? ¿Qué tal fue?), comprehensibility.

weeks.prep: World map, library books/websites. A Spanish article about Machu Picchu (e.g., from a tourism or encyclopedia site for students).
misconceptions: Placing Machu Picchu in Mexico or Chichén Itzá in Peru. Machu Picchu (Inca) is in Peru; Chichén Itzá (Maya) is in Mexico's Yucatán.
Copying research sentences in Spanish verbatim. Take notes in key words and rewrite.

days.guide: Locate eight sites and identify their landforms.

questions.q: Where is the Salar de Uyuni and what is it?
questions.a: In Bolivia; the world's largest salt flat.

questions.q: Who built Machu Picchu?
questions.a: The Inca, in the 1400s, in the Andes of Peru.

days.guide: Read the Machu Picchu article; answer questions.

questions.q: What does 'las ruinas' mean?

days.guide: Research one destination; take notes in Spanish.

questions.q: Write: 'Chichén Itzá is in Mexico; it has a famous pyramid.'
questions.a: Chichén Itzá está en México; tiene una pirámide famosa.

days.guide: Compare with a California landmark in six sentences.

questions.q: Write: 'Death Valley is hotter than Machu Picchu.'
questions.a: El Valle de la Muerte es más caluroso que Machu Picchu (or hace más calor en el Valle de la Muerte que en Machu Picchu).

days.guide: Give a 1-minute oral summary.

questions.q: What is 'el patrimonio' (as in Patrimonio de la Humanidad)?

weeks.assessment_key: Site key: Machu Picchu — Inca citadel (15th century) high in the Andes of Peru near Cusco, mountains; Chichén Itzá — Maya city with the pyramid El Castillo (Temple of Kukulcán), Yucatán Peninsula, Mexico, flat limestone plain with cenotes; Salar de Uyuni — world's largest salt flat, Bolivia, high plateau (Altiplano); El Yunque — tropical rainforest, Puerto Rico; La Alhambra — Moorish palace-fortress in Granada, Spain, on a hill below the Sierra Nevada. Oral summary rubric: 1 minute, 5+ facts in Spanish (location, landform, history, food, festival), pronunciation.

weeks.prep: Slides or a blog template; photos of the destination.
misconceptions: Listing events without sequence words. Use primero, luego, después, más tarde, por fin.
Mixing ir/ser preterite with present: 'Voy a Perú y fue…' — keep it all past.

days.guide: Teach sequencing words; outline a trip story.

questions.q: Write: 'First we went to Cusco, then we visited Machu Picchu.'
questions.a: Primero fuimos a Cusco, luego visitamos Machu Picchu.

days.guide: Draft a 15-sentence blog in the preterite.

questions.q: Write: 'Finally, I bought souvenirs.'

days.guide: Self-edit with a checklist; add photos.

questions.q: Correct: 'Yo pagé la cuenta.'

days.guide: Present and answer three questions.

questions.q: Answer: ¿Qué comiste allí?

days.guide: Give the unit 5 test.

questions.q: Translate: 'We arrived, ate lunch and then went to the beach.'
questions.a: Llegamos, almorzamos y después fuimos a la playa.

weeks.assessment_key: Travel blog rubric (1–4): 15 sentences in the preterite with sequencing words, regular -ar/-er/-ir and spelling-change forms, ir/ser, vacation vocabulary, cultural detail about the destination, photos with captions, accuracy. Unit 5 test: vacation vocabulary, regular and spelling-change preterite, -er/-ir preterite, ir/ser.

weeks.prep: Local volunteer listings (food bank, library, animal shelter, senior center). Short article about a youth volunteer project in Latin America.
misconceptions: Saying 'gente sin casa' — the standard phrase is 'la gente sin hogar' (homeless people).
Treating 'la gente' as plural: La gente es amable (singular verb).

days.guide: Learn 18 words; match to photos.

questions.q: What does 'donar' mean?
How do you say 'the elderly'?

days.guide: List local organizations; describe what each does.

questions.q: Write: 'At the food bank people collect food.'
questions.a: En el banco de comida la gente recoge comida.

days.guide: Read a youth volunteer article; summarize in five sentences.

questions.q: Write: 'The students helped the children.'
questions.a: Los estudiantes ayudaron a los niños.

days.guide: Survey family about volunteer work in the preterite.

questions.q: Ask: 'Did you volunteer last year?'

days.guide: Give the community vocabulary quiz.

questions.q: Translate: 'We recycled cans and bottles.'

weeks.assessment_key: Community vocabulary quiz: el trabajo voluntario (volunteer work), el centro de la comunidad, ayudar, los ancianos (elderly), la gente sin hogar, los niños, recoger (to pick up/collect), donar, reciclar, la basura, el hospital, el comedor de beneficencia (soup kitchen), el medio ambiente, la ropa usada, los juguetes, enseñar, la escuela primaria, el proyecto. Samples: We collected trash in the park → Recogimos basura en el parque; I donated clothes → Doné ropa. 80% proficient.

weeks.prep: Conjuguemos indirect object pronouns and dar.
misconceptions: Leaving out 'le' when the person is named. Spanish usually includes both: Le di el libro a Juan.
Confusing direct and indirect. Indirect answers 'to/for whom' (le, les); direct answers 'what' (lo, la).

days.guide: Teach IOPs; identify the indirect object in 15 sentences.

questions.q: In 'Mi mamá me compra una camisa,' what is the indirect object?
Which IOP replaces 'to my friends'?

days.guide: Teach dar present and preterite; drill.

questions.q: Conjugate dar (present) for yo.
Conjugate dar (preterite) for ella and ellos.

days.guide: Clarify le/les with a + person.

questions.q: Write: 'I gave the clothes to my grandmother.'
questions.a: Le di la ropa a mi abuela.

days.guide: Write 10 sentences about what you gave or did for others.

questions.q: Write: 'We gave food to the homeless people.'
questions.a: Les dimos comida a la gente sin hogar.

days.guide: Give the IOP and dar quiz.

questions.q: Translate: 'My teacher gave me a book.'
questions.a: Mi profesor(a) me dio un libro.

weeks.assessment_key: Quiz key: IOPs me, te, le, nos, os, les. Dar present: doy, das, da, damos, dais, dan; preterite: di, diste, dio, dimos, disteis, dieron (no accents). Samples: I gave the clothes to my grandma → Le di la ropa a mi abuela; She gave us food → Nos dio comida; They give toys to the children → Les dan juguetes a los niños; Did you give him the book? → ¿Le diste el libro? 80% proficient.

weeks.prep: StudySpanish.com irregular preterite pages. Read a bilingual short biography of César Chávez and Dolores Huerta.
misconceptions: Writing 'hico.' The él form is hizo (z keeps the 'th/s' sound).
Adding -ieron to decir: 'dijieron.' It's dijeron.

days.guide: Teach hacer preterite; answer ¿Qué hiciste ayer? 8 ways.

questions.q: Conjugate hacer for él.
Answer: ¿Qué hiciste ayer? (I made a cake)

days.guide: Teach decir; report what five people said with IOPs.

questions.q: Write: 'My friend told me that he went to the beach.'
questions.a: Mi amigo me dijo que fue a la playa.

questions.q: Conjugate decir for ellos.

days.guide: Complete StudySpanish practice.

questions.q: Conjugate hacer for nosotros.

days.guide: Read about Chávez and Huerta; write five preterite sentences.

questions.q: Write: 'César Chávez helped the farm workers.'
questions.a: César Chávez ayudó a los trabajadores del campo.

questions.q: What slogan did Dolores Huerta create?

days.guide: Give the irregular preterite quiz.

questions.q: Translate: 'What did they say?'

weeks.assessment_key: Quiz key: hacer — hice, hiciste, hizo, hicimos, hicisteis, hicieron; decir — dije, dijiste, dijo, dijimos, dijisteis, dijeron (no accents). Samples: ¿Qué (hacer) tú ayer? → hiciste; Ella me (decir) la verdad → dijo; Nosotros (hacer) la tarea → hicimos; Ellos nos (decir) 'gracias' → dijeron. Culture: César Chávez and Dolores Huerta co-founded the National Farm Workers Association (1962, later United Farm Workers), led the Delano grape strike and boycott (1965–1970) using nonviolence; Huerta coined '¡Sí, se puede!' 80% proficient.

weeks.prep: Materials for a small service project (food drive bags, cards for seniors, gloves and trash bags for a park cleanup). Camera.
misconceptions: Writing the report in present tense. It's a completed event: use the preterite.
Forgetting le/les with dar and decir: Les dimos…, Nos dijeron…

days.guide: Plan the service activity; write the plan in Spanish (Vamos a…).

questions.q: Write: 'We are going to collect food for the food bank.'
questions.a: Vamos a recoger comida para el banco de comida.

days.guide: Carry out the activity; take photos.

questions.q: What does 'juntar' mean?

days.guide: Write the 12-sentence preterite report.

questions.q: Write: 'We gave the cards to the elderly and they said thank you.'
questions.a: Les dimos las tarjetas a los ancianos y nos dijeron 'gracias'.

days.guide: Present with photos; answer questions.

questions.q: Answer: ¿Qué hicieron ustedes?
questions.a: Hicimos ___, e.g., Recogimos basura en el parque.

days.guide: Give the unit 6 test.

questions.q: Translate: 'I did a service project.'

weeks.assessment_key: Service report rubric (1–4): 12 sentences in the preterite describing plan, actions, what people said (decir) and what was given (dar + IOPs), uses hacer, community vocabulary, sequence words, photos; presentation clear. Unit 6 test: IOPs, dar, hacer, decir, community vocabulary.

weeks.prep: A Spanish-language TV guide (e.g., Univision or Telemundo listings). Genre words: la película de horror/terror, la comedia, el drama, la película de acción, la película de ciencia ficción, la película romántica, los dibujos animados, la telenovela, el programa de concursos, el programa deportivo, las noticias, el documental.
misconceptions: Saying 'Me parece que es emocionante' is correct; avoid 'Yo parece…' — parecer works like gustar: me parece.
Thinking telenovelas are just like U.S. soap operas. Telenovelas usually have a set ending after several months, unlike long-running soaps.

days.guide: Learn 12 genre words; classify 15 movies and shows.

questions.q: What genre is 'Toy Story'?

days.guide: Give opinions with me parece, creo que and adjectives.

questions.q: Write: 'Action movies seem exciting to me.'
questions.a: Las películas de acción me parecen emocionantes.

days.guide: Read a TV guide; answer questions on times, channels, genres.

questions.q: A listing says '20:00 Noticias.' What and when?

days.guide: Read about telenovelas; compare with U.S. dramas.

questions.q: Name two countries famous for telenovelas.
questions.a: Mexico and Colombia (also Venezuela, Brazil in Portuguese).

days.guide: Give the genre and opinions quiz.

questions.q: Translate: 'I think that cartoons are childish.'
questions.a: Creo que los dibujos animados son infantiles.

weeks.assessment_key: Genre and opinions quiz: classify movies/shows (e.g., Coco = dibujos animados/película animada; a news show = las noticias); opinions with me parece, creo que + adjectives emocionante, violento, tonto, infantil, divertido, aburrido, realista. Samples: I think horror movies are violent → Creo que las películas de horror son violentas; This program seems silly to me → Este programa me parece tonto. 80% proficient.

weeks.prep: A free Señor Wooly video. Verbs: aburrir, interesar, encantar, importar, faltar, doler.
misconceptions: Using a singular verb with plural things: 'Me aburre las películas.' Use aburren with plurals.
Conjugating acabar de with the second verb: 'Acabo de vi.' Use the infinitive: Acabo de ver.

days.guide: Teach acabar de + infinitive; 8 sentences.

questions.q: Write: 'We just ate.'
Write: 'She just watched a comedy.'
questions.a: Ella acaba de ver una comedia.

days.guide: Teach gustar-like verbs; write movie opinions.

questions.q: Write: 'Dramas bore me.'
Write: 'Science fiction interests my brother.'
questions.a: A mi hermano le interesa la ciencia ficción.

days.guide: Watch a Señor Wooly video; describe characters' likes/boredom/interests.

questions.q: Use 'interesar' about a character you saw.

days.guide: Discuss favorite movies with five gustar-like verbs.

questions.q: Ask: 'What kind of movies interest you?'

days.guide: Give the gustar-like verbs quiz.

questions.q: Translate: 'My feet hurt.'

weeks.assessment_key: Quiz key samples: Horror movies bore me → Me aburren las películas de horror; Documentaries interest us → Nos interesan los documentales; My head hurts → Me duele la cabeza; I just watched a movie → Acabo de ver una película; He is missing a ticket → Le falta un boleto; The environment matters to them → Les importa el medio ambiente. 80% proficient.

weeks.prep: A family film with Spanish audio and Spanish subtitles (e.g., Coco, 2017). Preview it. Phone for the video review.
misconceptions: Retelling the plot in present only. Use the preterite for completed events (Miguel encontró la guitarra).
Giving only opinions without plot support. Combine summary, opinion and evidence.

days.guide: Watch the film with Spanish audio/subtitles; take character notes.

questions.q: Who is the protagonist of Coco and what does he want?
questions.a: Miguel; he wants to be a musician.

days.guide: Write a 10-sentence preterite plot summary.

questions.q: Write: 'Miguel went to the Land of the Dead.'
questions.a: Miguel fue a la Tierra de los Muertos.

days.guide: Add opinions with gustar-like verbs and a star rating.

questions.q: Write: 'I loved the music; I give it five stars.'
questions.a: Me encantó la música; le doy cinco estrellas.

days.guide: Record a 2-minute video review.

questions.q: Say: 'I recommend this movie because it is exciting.'
questions.a: Recomiendo esta película porque es emocionante.

days.guide: Give the unit 7 test.

questions.q: Translate: 'I just saw a horror movie and it bored me.'
questions.a: Acabo de ver una película de horror y me aburrió.

weeks.assessment_key: Film review rubric (1–4): 10-sentence plot summary in the preterite, protagonist and characters named, opinions with gustar-like verbs and me parece, star rating with reasons, recommendation (Recomiendo esta película porque…), 2-minute video, pronunciation. Coco key facts if used: Miguel, a boy in Mexico who wants to be a musician though his family bans music, enters the Land of the Dead on Día de Muertos, meets Héctor, learns that Ernesto de la Cruz poisoned Héctor and stole his songs, discovers Héctor is his great-great-grandfather, and returns to help Mamá Coco remember her father. Unit 7 test: media vocabulary, acabar de, gustar-like verbs.

weeks.prep: Computer and phone for labeling; Conjuguemos e→i practice. Vocabulary: la computadora portátil, el teléfono celular, la pantalla, el teclado, el ratón, la impresora, el cargador, los audífonos, la red, navegar en la red, el correo electrónico, el sitio web, la contraseña, bajar/descargar, subir, la aplicación, el mensaje de texto, la cámara.
misconceptions: Treating pedir as e→ie: 'piedo.' Pedir and servir are e→i: pido, sirve.
Forgetting preterite stem change in third person for -ir stem-changers: pidió, pidieron; sirvió, sirvieron.

days.guide: Learn 18 tech words; label a computer and phone.

questions.q: How do you say 'password' and 'to download'?

days.guide: Teach e→i boot; Conjuguemos drill including pidió/sirvió.

questions.q: Conjugate pedir (present) for yo and nosotros.
Conjugate pedir (preterite) for él.

days.guide: Explain what 8 devices are for with servir para.

questions.q: Write: 'The phone is used to send messages.'
questions.a: El teléfono sirve para mandar mensajes.

days.guide: Survey family about daily screen use; write a report with numbers.

questions.q: Write: 'My mom uses the computer three hours a day.'
questions.a: Mi mamá usa la computadora tres horas al día.

days.guide: Give the technology and e→i quiz.

questions.q: Translate: 'The waiter served the food.'

weeks.assessment_key: Quiz key: pedir present — pido, pides, pide, pedimos, pedís, piden; preterite — pedí, pediste, pidió, pedimos, pedisteis, pidieron. Servir present — sirvo, sirves, sirve, servimos, servís, sirven; preterite third person sirvió, sirvieron. Samples: ¿Para qué sirve la impresora? → Sirve para imprimir; Mi hermano pidió un celular nuevo; Las computadoras sirven para escribir. 80% proficient.

weeks.prep: 20 sorting cards. Saber and conocer charts.
misconceptions: Using conocer for facts or skills: 'Conozco nadar.' Use saber + infinitive: Sé nadar.
Forgetting the personal a before people: Conozco a tu hermana.

days.guide: Teach saber vs conocer and the personal a; sort 20 sentences.

questions.q: Choose: Yo (sé/conozco) a la profesora.
Choose: ¿(Sabes/Conoces) dónde está el museo?

days.guide: Write 10 'Sé + infinitive' tech skills.

questions.q: Write: 'I know how to download apps.'

days.guide: Write about people and places you know with the personal a.

questions.q: Write: 'I know your parents.'

days.guide: Interview a parent with both verbs.

questions.q: Ask: 'Do you know how to use this app?'

days.guide: Give the saber/conocer quiz.

questions.q: Give the yo form of conocer and saber.

weeks.assessment_key: Quiz key: saber — sé, sabes, sabe, sabemos, sabéis, saben (facts, information, how to + infinitive); conocer — conozco, conoces, conoce, conocemos, conocéis, conocen (people, places, familiarity) with personal a before people. Samples: I know how to make a web page → Sé crear una página web; Do you know Madrid? → ¿Conoces Madrid?; We know your cousin → Conocemos a tu primo; She knows the password → Ella sabe la contraseña. 80% proficient.

weeks.prep: A Spanish infographic on teen internet use in Spain or Mexico (search 'infografía uso de internet adolescentes'). U.S. teen data (e.g., Pew Research Center).
misconceptions: Making claims without numbers in the comparison. Cite the data: 'El 90% de los jóvenes…'
Debating with 'sí/no' only. Use en mi opinión, creo que, estoy de acuerdo, no estoy de acuerdo porque…

days.guide: Read the infographic; answer data questions.

questions.q: Say '85 percent of teens use social media.'
questions.a: El ochenta y cinco por ciento de los jóvenes usa las redes sociales.

days.guide: Compare with U.S. data in six sentences.

questions.q: Write: 'More teens in the U.S. have phones than in…'
questions.a: Más jóvenes en Estados Unidos tienen teléfono celular que en ___.

days.guide: Write a 10-sentence opinion piece on phones for teens.

questions.q: Give one ventaja and one desventaja in Spanish.
questions.a: Una ventaja: Los celulares sirven para comunicarse con la familia. Una desventaja: Pueden causar distracción o problemas para dormir.

days.guide: Hold a short debate.

questions.q: Disagree politely with a reason.
questions.a: No estoy de acuerdo porque los teléfonos son útiles para estudiar.

days.guide: Give the unit 8 test.

questions.q: Translate: 'In my opinion, teens should know how to protect their password.'
questions.a: En mi opinión, los jóvenes deben saber proteger su contraseña.

weeks.assessment_key: Opinion piece rubric (1–4): 10 sentences, clear opinion, 2+ ventajas and 2+ desventajas, data or examples, opinion phrases (en mi opinión, creo que, por un lado/por otro lado), conclusion, accuracy. Unit 8 test: technology vocabulary, pedir/servir, saber/conocer. Debate: uses agreement/disagreement phrases and gives reasons.

weeks.prep: Flashcards, Conjuguemos, picture for description task.
misconceptions: Applying stem changes to nosotros. Review the boot.
Mixing DOP and IOP: 'Lo di a ella.' Use Se lo di only in Spanish II; for now: Le di el libro.

days.guide: Timed Conjuguemos regular present drill.

questions.q: Conjugate escribir for nosotros and hablar for ellos.

days.guide: Review irregulars and all stem-changers.

questions.q: Conjugate tener, venir and poder for yo.
Conjugate servir for ella.

days.guide: Review tú commands and progressive with picture description.

questions.q: Command: 'Tell the truth.'
Say: 'They are sleeping.'

days.guide: 20-item DOP/IOP practice.

questions.q: Replace the object: Veo la película.
Translate: 'I write him a letter.'

days.guide: Self-scored practice test; list weak areas.

questions.q: Which stem-change type is 'preferir'?

weeks.assessment_key: Present-tense practice test self-scored with keys from prior weeks: regular -ar/-er/-ir; ser, estar, ir, tener, venir; o→ue (puedo, duermo), e→ie (quiero, prefiero), e→i (pido, sirvo); tú commands (regular = él form; irregular di, haz, ve, pon, sal, sé, ten, ven); progressive (estar + -ando/-iendo); DOPs (lo, la, los, las) and IOPs (me, te, le, nos, les). Weakest areas listed with a plan.

weeks.prep: Unit tests, travel blog, self-made culture quiz, two authentic texts (a blog post and an ad).
misconceptions: Mixing preterite forms of ir/ser with other verbs. Practice in stories.
Forgetting accents on regular preterite yo and él forms (compré, compró).

days.guide: Narrative writing reviewing regular and spelling-change preterite.

questions.q: Write: 'I arrived, looked for my friends and played soccer.'
questions.a: Llegué, busqué a mis amigos y jugué al fútbol.

days.guide: Story retelling with ir/ser, hacer, decir, dar.

questions.q: Write: 'She went to the store, made a cake and gave it to me.'
questions.a: Ella fue a la tienda, hizo un pastel y me lo dio (or y me dio el pastel).

days.guide: Culture review with a self-made quiz.

questions.q: What is the Rastro?

days.guide: Read a blog post and an ad; answer questions.

questions.q: On an ad, what does 'oferta' mean?

days.guide: Mock 5-minute conversation on all topics.

questions.q: Answer: ¿Qué hiciste el fin de semana pasado?
questions.a: El fin de semana pasado ___ (preterite), e.g., fui al cine y comí con mi familia.

weeks.assessment_key: Self-scored practice tasks: narrative uses regular and spelling-change preterite correctly; story retelling uses fui/fue, hice/hizo, dije/dijo, di/dio; culture quiz answers (tapas = small shared plates in Spain; huipiles = Maya woven blouses; azotea = rooftop terrace; Machu Picchu = Inca, Peru; telenovelas = serial dramas with a set ending); reading questions answered with evidence; mock 5-minute conversation covers present and past.

weeks.prep: Final exam packet: an authentic text and a native-speaker clip with comprehension and inference questions you write ahead; Spanish I can-do checklist.
misconceptions: Answering inference questions with only literal facts. Explain what the text suggests using evidence.
Using only present tense in the narrative. A memorable day requires the preterite for events.

days.guide: Read an authentic text and listen to a clip; answer comprehension and inference questions.

questions.q: How do you answer an inference question?
questions.a: State what the text suggests and support it with a detail from the text or audio.

days.guide: 5-minute unscripted conversation.

questions.q: Answer: ¿Cómo es tu casa?
questions.a: Mi casa es ___ y tiene ___ dormitorios; mi cuarto es más ___ que ___.

days.guide: Write a 15–20 sentence narrative of a memorable day.

questions.q: Write an opening in the preterite.
questions.a: Example: El verano pasado fui a la playa con mi familia.

days.guide: Present a 2-minute cultural comparison.

questions.q: Give one comparison sentence.
questions.a: Example: En España la cena es más tarde que en mi casa.

days.guide: Complete the Spanish I can-do self-assessment; set Spanish II goals.

questions.q: Write a can-do statement.
questions.a: Example: 'I can describe a past trip using the preterite.'

weeks.assessment_key: Integrated performance assessment rubric (1–4 each): Interpretive — main idea, key details and one supported inference; Interpersonal — 5-minute unscripted conversation on home, shopping, a past trip and technology with questions and follow-ups (Novice High: strings of sentences, some past tense); Presentational writing — 15–20 sentences narrating a memorable day using present for background and preterite for events, sequence words, varied verbs, accurate agreement; Presentational speaking — 2-minute cultural comparison with specific details. Proficient = 3s across; completes Spanish I.
